mainEntity.name: How long do porcelain veneers last when used to correct uneven edges?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain veneers typically last 10-15 years with proper care and maintenance. Their longevity depends on factors such as oral hygiene, eating habits, and whether underlying issues like grinding are properly managed. Regular dental check-ups help monitor the condition of veneers and identify any maintenance needs early. Avoiding hard foods and protecting teeth from grinding can help maximise the lifespan of veneer restorations.

mainEntity.name: Are there alternatives to veneers for correcting uneven tooth edges?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several alternatives exist depending on the specific situation. Dental bonding using tooth-coloured resin can address minor irregularities more conservatively and at lower cost. Tooth contouring or reshaping might suffice for small adjustments. Crowns may be necessary for extensively damaged teeth, whilst orthodontic treatment could address underlying alignment issues contributing to uneven wear patterns.

mainEntity.name: Can veneers be placed if I grind my teeth at night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Teeth grinding doesn't necessarily prevent veneer placement, but it requires careful management. Most dentists recommend using a custom night guard to protect veneers from excessive forces during sleep. The underlying grinding habit should be addressed through stress management, bite adjustment, or other appropriate treatments. Proper protection allows many patients with bruxism to successfully maintain veneer restorations long-term.

mainEntity.name: Will correcting uneven edges with veneers affect my bite?

acceptedAnswer.text: When properly planned and executed, veneer treatment should improve bite function rather than compromise it. Experienced dentists carefully evaluate your existing bite relationships and design veneers to enhance both appearance and function. Temporary adjustments during healing are normal, but persistent bite problems should be addressed promptly to prevent complications and ensure comfortable long-term function.

mainEntity.name: How much tooth structure needs to be removed for veneer placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Typically, 0.3-0.7mm of enamel is removed from the front surface of teeth to accommodate veneer thickness. This minimal preparation preserves most of the natural tooth structure whilst creating space for the porcelain restoration. The exact amount varies based on the degree of correction needed and the specific case requirements. Modern techniques focus on conservative preparation whenever possible.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a veneer chips or breaks on the biting edge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor chips can sometimes be polished smooth or repaired with bonding material, whilst more significant damage usually requires veneer replacement. The extent of repair options depends on the size and location of the damage. Avoiding hard foods, wearing night guards if prescribed, and maintaining regular dental visits help prevent damage and address any issues promptly when they occur.
